subject: Renewal negotiation: capacity safety-net & tail-latency clause
messages:
From: Alicia Patel <ap@finbridge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Hayes <devon.hayes@finbridge.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation — reliability conditions and addendum request

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the quick chat last week. As we head into our renewal window (contract expires 2026-09-30), the execs are asking for a clearer path on reliability obligations before we commit to expansion. A few concrete asks from FinBridge: 

- An explicit capacity safety-net for peak windows (our busiest 2% of traffic) — we saw sustained token-processing queuing in June and July.
- A tail-latency credit mechanism tied to p99.9/p99.95 spikes (we'd prefer credits rather than one-off goodwill) so we can model risk into our budget.
- A regional uptime target or fallback routing guarantee for our east-1 users.

We'd like to propose an addendum to the existing SOW that: 1) documents the safety-net and pilot for Dedicated capacity; 2) defines a clear credit formula for tail-latency breaches; and 3) includes a short testing window for the fallback routing. Attached is a short summary from our reliability team and examples of the events we saw.

Can your team draft a proposal we can review by next Tuesday (2026-08-25)? Procurement (cc'd) will need high-level commercial terms to estimate reserves.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, FinBridge
ap@finbridge.com

Attachments: finbridge_reliability_highlights_Aug2026.pdf (summary)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Patel <ap@finbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — reliability conditions and addendum request

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear asks and the summary. I appreciate the urgency and agree we should have a documented path before renewal.

I'll have Ben pull a commercial-first draft of an SLA addendum that covers: safety-net language, a candidate credit schedule for p99/p99.9/p99.95, and a proposal for a short Dedicated-capacity pilot. Marissa will validate the operational feasibility and provide the p99 baselines from our telemetry.

Ben/Marissa — can you take the lead on a draft and target delivery EOD Tue (2026-08-25)? If it helps, we can include a conditional timeline: if pilot acceptance is agreed by 2026-09-15 we can bind the addendum to the renewal.

Alicia — one quick ask from our side: could you share the specific time windows and the sample traces you referenced (2% busiest windows)? Devon/procurement in CC — if you can flag any internal constraints up-front that would speed approvals.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Patel <ap@finbridge.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: SLA addendum outline and credit construct (attached)

Hi Alicia / Devon / Procurement team —

Attached is a first-pass PDF (SLA_proposed_addendum_v2.pdf) and a supporting CSV with p99 analysis. High level summary below:

1) Capacity safety-net
   - Redwood will provision a Dedicated pilot pool for FinBridge covering up to 15% above your historical 97th percentile throughput during scheduled peak windows for the pilot period (30 days).
   - If pilot runbook is accepted, a Reserved Capacity commitment can be scoped into the renewal with a 90-day ramp.

2) Tail-latency credit formula (proposal)
   - Define baseline p99/p99.9/p99.95 from prior 90 days (we propose the attached baseline).
   - Credit = min(10% of monthly invoice, (observed_excess_ms / baseline_ms) * 5% of monthly invoice) for each calendar-day where p99.95 > baseline * 1.5.
   - Credits calculated monthly and applied against the following invoice.

3) Regional fallback guarantee
   - Redwood will implement automatic fallback routing to an alternate region for east-1 traffic when observed regional availability drops below 99.6% for a rolling 60-minute period.
   - Fallback testing window: 2x 4-hour maintenance windows agreed by both parties during pilot.

Open questions for FinBridge:
- Do you prefer a capped dollar credit (we proposed 10% cap) or an uncapped measurable SLA credit?
- Which exact windows constitute your 2% busiest periods (we need UTC ranges).

If this looks directionally correct, we can iterate language and ship a DocuSign-ready addendum.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call today if you want to walk through the formula.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: SLA_proposed_addendum_v2.pdf, p99_tail_latency_analysis_aug2026.csv
From: Alicia Patel <ap@finbridge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Hayes <devon.hayes@finbridge.com>, FinBridge Procurement <procurement@finbridge.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: SLA addendum outline and credit construct (attached)

Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear draft. A few counterpoints from FinBridge reliability & procurement: 

- We prefer a deterministic, uncapped credit schedule for p99.95 breaches tied to observed user impact (we understand cost exposure, but uncapped credits are what our finance team requires for enterprise vendor risk).
- The 15% pilot headroom is reasonable if we get guaranteed isolation during our peak windows. That isolation needs to include KV cache persistence guarantees for session affinity.
- For regional fallback: the routing guarantee is helpful, but we'd like a firm RTO for failover (max 3 minutes to route to alternate region) and a runbook for reconciling cross-region consistency.

Procurement: we can accept a 10% monthly cap on non-SLA commercial credits if the p99.95 credit schedule remains uncapped for customer-impacting events. We will flag that in redlines.

Attached is a short note from our procurement team outlining acceptable language and the internal approval path.

Can your ops team (Marissa / Grace) confirm feasibility of: KV cache persistence, 3-min RTO for failover, and an acceptance test for Dedicated isolation?

Regards,
Alicia Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, FinBridge

Attachments: finbridge_procurement_constraints_aug2026.docx
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Patel <ap@finbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, FinBridge Procurement <procurement@finbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: SLA addendum outline and credit construct (attached)

Alicia / Devon / Procurement —

Thanks for the detailed feedback and the procurement note. Internal update after ops review: Marissa and Grace validated the majority of asks; a few clarifications and our counterproposal below.

- Isolation & pilot: We can provision a Dedicated pilot with isolation controls (reserved GPU pools, namespace-level KV reservations) and an acceptance test suite. Proposed pilot length: 30 days with up to 2 agreed maintenance windows for fallback validation.

- KV cache persistence: We confirm session-affinity cache persistence for the pilot (best-effort persistence across pod restarts during the pilot; for full durability we’ll include a recommended config change and an HLD in the pilot runbook).

- Failover RTO: We are confident we can meet a 3-minute routing failover for the fallback path when the alternate region is warm. To operationalize this we propose:
  * Warm standby nodes in alternate region during your peak windows (cost-sharing during pilot to be defined).
  * A measured failover test (3-minute target) during acceptance. If we fail more than 2/4 tests, the credit multiplier increases per the uncovered events.

- Credit construct: We acknowledge FinBridge preference for an uncapped event-based credit tied to customer-impacting p99.95 spikes. Our compromise: uncapped credits for events classified as "major customer-impacting outages" (definition in the addendum), and a capped (10% monthly) buffer for transitory tail-latency degradations that do not meet the major outage threshold. We will draft precise thresholds and detection rules in the addendum.

Next steps (proposed timeline):
- 2026-09-03: Redwood sends updated addendum language + defined detection rules
- 2026-09-06: FinBridge provides final redlines from procurement
- 2026-09-09: Kickoff for Dedicated pilot if redlines acceptable; pilot runs 30 days
- Renewal decision point maintained at 2026-09-30, with pilot acceptance gating reserved-capacity incorporation.

Ben will circulate the updated addendum and a DocuSign-ready file on 2026-09-03. Can procurement confirm if the above timeline works for approvals? If so, we'll route legal and schedule the kickoff.

Thanks all — we want to make sure the renewal is a constructive step forward, not just a transactional renewal.

Warmly,
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
